verses.text: Pharao therefore charged all his people, saying: Whatsoever shall be born of the male sex, ye shall cast into the river: whatsoever of the female, ye shall save alive.
verses.note: Pharao orders every newborn Hebrew boy cast into the river.

verses.text: After this there went a man of the house of Levi; and took a wife of his own kindred.
verses.note: A man of the house of Levi takes a wife of his own kindred.

verses.text: And she conceived, and bore a son; and seeing him a goodly child hid him three months.
verses.note: She bears a son, sees that he is goodly, and hides him three months.

verses.text: And when she could hide him no longer, she took a basket made of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and pitch: and put the little babe therein, and laid him in the sedges by the river's brink,
verses.note: When she can hide him no longer she lays him in a basket of bulrushes among the sedges by the river's brink.

verses.text: His sister standing afar off, and taking notice what would be done.
verses.note: His sister stands afar off to see what will be done.

verses.text: And behold the daughter of Pharao came down to wash herself in the river: and her maids walked by the river's brink. And when she saw the basket in the sedges, she sent one of her maids for it: and when it was brought,
verses.note: Pharao's daughter comes down to the river and sends her maid for the basket.

verses.text: She opened it and seeing within it an infant crying, having compassion on it she said: This is one of the babes of the Hebrews.
verses.note: She sees the crying infant and has compassion on him.

verses.text: And the child's sister said to her Shall I go and call to thee a Hebrew woman, to nurse the babe?
verses.note: The child's sister offers to call a Hebrew woman to nurse him.

verses.text: She answered: Go. The maid went and called her mother.
verses.note: Pharao's daughter says Go, and the maid calls the child's mother.

verses.text: And Pharao's daughter said to her. Take this child and nurse him for me: I will give thee thy wages. The woman took, and nursed the child: and when he was grown up, she delivered him to Pharao's daughter.
verses.note: Pharao's daughter pays the child's own mother to nurse him.

verses.text: And she adopted him for a son, and called him Moses, saying: Because I took him out of the water.
verses.note: She adopts him and names him Moses, because she took him out of the water.

verses.text: But come, and I will send thee to Pharao, that thou mayst bring forth my people, the children of Israel out of Egypt.
verses.note: Years later God sends Moses to Pharao to bring his people out of Egypt.

verses.text: And when he was exposed, Pharao's daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.
verses.note: Stephen recalls that Pharao's daughter took the exposed child up and raised him as her own son.

verses.text: And Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians; and he was mighty in his words and in his deeds.
verses.note: Stephen says Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians.

verses.text: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months by his parents; because they saw he was a comely babe, and they feared not the king's edict.
verses.note: Hebrews praises the faith of Moses' parents, who hid him and did not fear the king's edict.
